shortDescription: West African crude oil differentials edged lower on Thursday after a recent jump driven by disruption to Middle East supply.

children: West African crude oil differentials edged lower on Thursday after a recent jump driven by disruption to Middle East supply.

Nigerian grades such as Bonga and Forcados should be trading at around plus $5 to dated Brent, a trade source said, adding that the market was changing fast. Earlier this week, grades were estimated to be trading at plus $6 to dated Brent.

Freight rates on some key routes for West African crude in August moved back to the multi-year highs reached during the early stages of the U.S.-Israeli war on Iran, according to Riverlake data, though they have since eased slightly.
Nigeria could double investment into its energy sector within five years after joining the International Energy Agency, its chief Fatih Birol said.

Russia will slightly reduce its oil output this year, Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Novak said, but the situation is temporary and oil production will begin to increase once domestic refineries finish scheduled maintenance.

The country has meanwhile shipped more than 10 million barrels of crude oil via the Northern Sea Route so far this year, up from 13 million barrels for the whole of last year, boosting supplies to China, two trade sources said and LSEG shipping data showed. China is a key buyer of West African crude.
